title: Tenki Sandbox
description: Gives agents a disposable Tenki Sandbox Linux VM for running code and shell commands, editing files and working with git repositories.
Every tool call shares one session, created on first use; opt-in tool groups add port exposure, persistent volumes, snapshots and remote access.

tenki.apikey.title: API Key
tenki.apikey.description: Tenki workspace API key (starts with tk_), from the API Keys screen in the Tenki console.

tenki.github_token.title: GitHub Token
tenki.github_token.description: Optional GitHub token that lets git clone private repositories. Tenki makes it available inside the sandbox as the GH_TOKEN and GIT_TOKEN environment variables, so any command the agent runs can read it: use a fine-grained, read-only token limited to the repositories the agent needs.

tenki.base_url.title: API URL
tenki.base_url.description: Tenki Sandbox API endpoint. Leave empty for the default (https://api.tenki.cloud).

tenki.cpu_cores.title: CPU Cores
tenki.cpu_cores.description: Virtual CPUs for the sandbox VM.

tenki.memory_mb.title: Memory (MB)
tenki.memory_mb.description: Memory for the sandbox VM, in MB. Tenki requires an even number.

tenki.disk_size_gb.title: Disk Size (GB)
tenki.disk_size_gb.description: Root disk size, in GB. 5 is Tenki's default; Tenki recommends 20 for agents that clone repositories and install dependencies.

tenki.idle_timeout_minutes.title: Idle Timeout (minutes)
tenki.idle_timeout_minutes.description: Tenki pauses the session after this many minutes without activity. A pause keeps memory and files under /home/tenki but clears /tmp; it does not terminate the session.

tenki.max_duration_minutes.title: Max Duration (minutes)
tenki.max_duration_minutes.description: Upper bound on the session's lifetime, set when it is created: the cost backstop if the pipeline never shuts the session down, for example after an engine crash.

tenki.exec_timeout_secs.title: Execution Timeout (seconds)
tenki.exec_timeout_secs.description: Max seconds a single run_command/run_code call may take.

tenki.max_output_chars.title: Max Output (characters)
tenki.max_output_chars.description: Output longer than this is truncated before being returned to the agent.

tenki.image.title: Image
tenki.image.description: Registry image to start the sandbox from, such as a template build like myworkspace/my-node-env. Leave empty for Tenki's base image.

tenki.toolGroups.title: Tool groups
tenki.toolGroups.description: Which groups of Tenki Sandbox tools this node publishes to the agent. This node implements 22 tools across 7 groups, and every extra tool makes the right one harder for an LLM to pick, so only the listed groups are exposed. Leave this empty for the recommended set: execution, filesystem and git (11 tools), enough to run code, edit files and work in a repository. Use all to publish all 22. Naming groups replaces the default set rather than adding to it, and a value that names only unknown groups stops the pipeline at startup rather than widening back to the defaults. The other groups are deliberate opt-ins: ports publishes a sandbox service at a public URL, volumes attaches workspace storage that other sessions share and that outlives this session, snapshots creates billed storage that also outlives it, and remote_access exchanges raw bytes with processes inside the VM instead of returning structured results.

enum: Remote access (2, opt-in: raw byte streams)
